Overview:
KARL MAYER is a mechanical engineering company that offers a wide range of products and services of its sector with the focus on textile machinery building. The business activities are concentrated on the fields of warp knitting, technical textiles and warp preparation for weaving. KARL MAYER supports the success of its international customers with products and services that are outstanding in both economic and technical terms, as well as with innovations that move the textile world forward. KARL MAYER has employees all over the world. Thanks to its global organization and its claim to produce in its main markets, the company is always close to its customers and their needs. Today, it has subsidiaries in the USA, India, Italy, Hong Kong, Japan, China, Turkey, India and Switzerland, as well as agencies in all parts of the world. KARL MAYER is a German family-owned company, which has focused on financial independence and economic sustainability since its foundation in 1937. As a permanent, reliable partner with decades of experience and a high level of quality in all areas, it supports the competitiveness of its customers and business partners. title: Karl Mayer to celebrate 75th anniversary - Knitting Industry
content: Leading German warp knitting machine builder Karl Mayer is busy making preparations with its employees and customers to celebrate its 75th year in business. Each sector has its leader and Karl Mayer is certainly the leader in the field of warp knitting. "When our company took up the production of warp knitting machines in 1947, nobody could foresee how much the production an. “When our company took up the production of warp knitting machines in 1947, nobody could foresee how much the production and number of employees would increase,” stated Karl Mayer in 1960. “Today we employ 1200 operatives in the largest factory in our sector; we had to expand the production equipment continually in order to set up the most up-to-date machine tools and to configure the production as rationally as possible until we reached the present monthly capacity of 140-150 warp knitting machines,” added the company’s founder in his statement to commemorate the delivery of the 5000th machine from its works¹.

title: Karl Mayer celebrates 35 years of EL pattern drive
content: OBERSHAUSEN, Germany – Karl Mayer is marking a milestone this year: on Nov. 30, 1990, the company delivered its first warp knitting machine with electronic guide bar control, the KS 4 EL. The SU drive, first used in Multibar Raschel machines, controlled the shogging movement of the guide bars magneto-mechanically through actuators and a microcomputer. A version of the SU drive with an integrated overlap device, developed in 1985, also allowed tricot machines to eliminate pattern chains and discs, clearing the way for further electronic advancements. To overcome the mechanical limitations of the SU drive on tricot machines, Karl Mayer developed an electrically powered system, breaking new ground in the process. The prototype led to the first electronic guide bar control system, launching a new era. After an upgrade for high-bar models, the first Multibar Raschel machine with electronic control of all guide bars — the TL 66 — debuted in 2002.
